UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE, Plaintiff, v. KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6, Defendants. ____________________________________/ | Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

[PROPOSED] ORDER

This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff’s Motion Under Rule 26(d)(1) for Present Authorization to Serve Two Interrogatories on Meta Concerning Plaintiff’s Full Legal Name and Facebook Account (the “Motion”). The Court has considered the Motion, the Memorandum in Support, Exhibit A — Meta — November 7, 2026 — Final (“Exhibit A”), the Declaration of Marvelle J. Ballentine with its Exhibit 1, any opposition and reply, and the standard applicable under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(d)(1). The Court has considered Plaintiff’s request for prompt determination on the papers and his request that this authorization be resolved before or expressly within any adverse disposition that would depend on the specific reporting fact addressed by Exhibit A. The Court finds that authorization is warranted. The Court makes no finding on the merits of any claim or defense. Accordingly, it is hereby

ORDERED that the Motion is GRANTED; it is further

ORDERED that, as an express and limited exception to the discovery posture described in ECF No. 108, and notwithstanding the denial of Plaintiff’s previous requests in ECF No. 84, Plaintiff is authorized under Rule 26(d)(1) to serve on Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta”), before the Rule 26(f) conference, the two interrogatories set out in Exhibit A, which is adopted by reference and which concerns (1) whether Meta submitted to NCMEC, between July 1, 2022 and April 22, 2026, inclusive, any CyberTipline report that, as submitted by Meta, contained or otherwise identified the full legal name “Marvelle J. Ballentine,” and (2) whether Meta submitted to NCMEC, in the same inclusive period, any CyberTipline report in connection with the Facebook account associated with Plaintiff and enforced against on or about July 4, 2022; it is further

ORDERED that this authorization extends only to the two interrogatories in Exhibit A and does not commence general discovery; it is further

ORDERED that Plaintiff shall serve Exhibit A on Meta within three (3) days after entry of this Order; it is further

ORDERED that Meta shall serve its answers and any objections within seven (7) days after service of Exhibit A [or: on or before ____________, 2026]; it is further

ORDERED that Meta shall answer through an officer or agent furnishing information available to Meta under Rule 33(b)(1)(B), under oath under Rule 33(b)(3), with any objection stated with specificity under Rule 33(b)(4) and an answer to the extent not objected to, and with the signatures Rule 33(b)(5) requires, subject to the answer and content limits stated in Exhibit A, including a concise qualification necessary for accuracy; it is further

ORDERED that this Order authorizes no production of any CyberTipline report and requires no filing of the answers; that any later use of the answers or of the Declaration on any pending motion remains subject to Rule 12(d) and to any applicable confidentiality or sealing requirements; and that this Order does not decide the truth of the April 22, 2026 letters, any wrongdoing, any agreement, any fault, any statutory exception, or any damages, and does not deem any answer an admission of liability or a basis for dismissal; it is further

ORDERED that this Order supplies the defined prospective relief requested in the Motion, does not adjudicate the matters pending in ECF Nos. 89, 93, 112, 113, and 118 through 123, and does not deem any earlier request satisfied.

Alexandria, Virginia

__________, 2026

______________________________

United States District Judge
